content.comment_body: Good afternoon. I downloaded the file, but it's either empty or I can't open it. How can I display the normal number instead of the hexadecimal format with #? Thank you.
Hello [user_name], this forum operates in English. Please post your questions in English next time. Thank you. Which file are you referring to?
In the web editor, how do you remove the hexadecimal number (#) so that the time appears in a normal format? For example, instead of 16# 22 h, it should display as 22h. Thank you.
If you do not speak English, consider using Google Translate.
Did you see the link to another topic above? How can you remove the hex marking (16#) when showing switch times for a weekly timer in the extended web server?

Hello, I downloaded a link explaining how to modify the weekly timer in the web editor using hexadecimal numbers. I tried it and it works. Thank you. I found another link about removing the hex number. I downloaded that file several times but either can't open it or it's empty. I am only an IT professional. Thanks and regards.

I used Google Translate. Whenever I post here, my English text is automatically translated to Spanish. I'm not very skilled with computers. I downloaded information about how to modify the weekly timer in the web editor using hexadecimal, and it worked for me. Thank you. I also saw another file about removing the hex notation. I've tried downloading it several times, but I can't open it or it's empty. I apologize for any inconvenience. Thank you and greetings.
Unfortunately, I am not sure which file you mean. Please be more specific.

Hexadecimal time format can be problematic. You cannot use the hh:mm format in a single I/O field—you must use two fields, one for each byte. See the attached example for reference. To remove the '#' symbol, refer to the topic: "How can you remove the hex marking (16#) when displaying weekly timer switch times in the extended web server?" Attachment: Weekly timer example.zip (82 downloads)
Which file are you unable to open— the project file or the LSC file?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering difficulties accessing downloadable support files intended to help modify the weekly timer display format in a web editor. Specifically, downloaded files are either empty or cannot be opened, leading to frustration. The user also feels confused about interpreting or converting the hexadecimal time notation within the web editor and prefers to display standard hour values. Language barriers and unclear file references further complicate communication and troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects support files to be straightforward to download and open, containing clear instructions for changing the timer display from hexadecimal to standard time format in the web editor. They are looking for easy-to-follow solutions for removing hexadecimal flags and displaying normal hour notation within the editor.
